name: Lumina coworking platform
overview: A normalized relational model separates members, product plans, subscription history, spaces, shared amenities, reservations, and invoices. An associative table represents shared amenities. Financial and reservation history remain linked to anonymizable member records.

assumptions: The demonstration is deliberately scoped: locations are labels with no address/manager facts; introduce a locations entity if those attributes become requirements.
All timestamps represent UTC; timezone conversion occurs at the client boundary.
A member can have historical memberships. Transactional policy prevents overlapping active membership intervals.
Amounts use USD and invoices are standalone billed totals, not aggregates of unstored invoice-line records.
Included hours are a plan allowance; consumption accounting and payment processing are outside this specified sample scope.
Plans should be versioned rather than mutating prices that need historical interpretation.
Identifiers are assigned explicitly by the application, not by a sequence.
businessRules: Unique member emails, plan names, amenity names, invoice numbers, and space names within a location are enforced by UNIQUE keys.
Positive capacity, nonnegative amounts/hours/rates, permitted lifecycle states, and ordered dates are enforced with CHECK constraints.
Foreign keys retain member/booking/invoice history through RESTRICT/NO ACTION. Only pure amenity links cascade.

No overlapping confirmed bookings: the application must lock the space row and query intersecting intervals in the same transaction before insertion. For SQLite use BEGIN IMMEDIATE and serialize writes. Row-level CHECK constraints do not enforce this cross-row rule.
Back-to-back bookings are valid half-open intervals. Cancelled bookings do not block availability.
Member data access and location-scoped staff access require application authorization; invoice visibility is limited to billing administrators.
Member contact details can be anonymized while the member identifier and invoices remain for seven-year billing retention.
Changing booking and invoice status requires an authorized atomic transaction; payment processing uses idempotency at the integration boundary.
security: No passwords, payment cards, or real personal data are seeded. Example contact addresses use example.org.
Separate member, location-staff, and billing-administrator permissions in the application and production database roles.
Encrypt transport and backups; minimize contact data and audit access to billing information.
Retain invoices seven years and booking history two years; anonymize member contact information without breaking retained FKs.
Member phone numbers are optional private contact details; restrict access and include them in anonymization.
